bug_semantics: Angular SSR reconstructed the request's absolute base URL from attacker-controlled Host and X-Forwarded-* headers without syntax or destination validation, then used that URL as the server-rendering origin and exposed the request to application code. An attacker able to supply those headers could therefore steer relative HttpClient requests or application-built requests to an attacker-selected external or internal host, with malformed host/path/port values also enabling header or URL injection behavior.
flaw_origin: Commit 3c9697a8c34a5e0f3470bde73f11f9f32107f42e introduced the current hybrid-rendering request pipeline in packages/angular/ssr/src/request.ts: createRequestUrl selected x-forwarded-proto, x-forwarded-host/host/:authority, and x-forwarded-port directly from IncomingMessage and constructed the absolute URL without validation. The same commit passed that Request both as the Angular render URL and through the REQUEST injection token. Its parent ad4c782e2466007c9f29142503b29247b07a204c has none of request.ts, app-engine.ts, or tokens.ts, so this is the atomic first write for the current @angular/ssr lineage rather than the later moves, forwarding-header refinements, or fix. The repository also preserves an older @nguniversal Express lineage, but that implementation was removed before this independent current-lineage first write and is not substituted for the BIC fixed here.
ai_marker: absent: the BIC commit object names Alan Agius <alanagius@google.com> as author and Alan Agius <alan.agius4@gmail.com> as committer; its message has no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, or other AI marker
evidence: Official CVE.org CVEList v5 object for CVE-2026-27739 is PUBLISHED and identifies GHSA-x288-3778-4hhx, the Host/X-Forwarded-* SSRF mechanism, affected ranges, and fix PR https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/pull/32516; it is not withdrawn or rejected.

git show 3c9697a8c34a5e0f3470bde73f11f9f32107f42e -- packages/angular/ssr/src/request.ts shows the new createRequestUrl reading x-forwarded-proto, x-forwarded-host/host/:authority, and x-forwarded-port and calling new URL with the resulting unvalidated origin; packages/angular/ssr/src/render.ts passes request.url to renderAngular and supplies the same Request as REQUEST.

Direct parent-tree checks with git cat-file -e ad4c782e2466007c9f29142503b29247b07a204c:<path> report ABSENT for packages/angular/ssr/src/request.ts, packages/angular/ssr/src/app-engine.ts, and packages/angular/ssr/src/tokens.ts; the BIC creates all three, establishing parent absence rather than relying on blame.

git cat-file commit 3c9697a8c34a5e0f3470bde73f11f9f32107f42e gives the sole parent ad4c782e2466007c9f29142503b29247b07a204c, human author/committer identities, and no AI attribution trailer; the commit is non-merge and has no reconstructable squash-member indication.

History cross-check distinguishes later changes: ad1d7d76fc6b94b8f12841fcfb331e5fb098403e refined proxy-header/port handling, and 7be6c8f0e2883c85546eb1691c91fa7d4aefc0d3 changed URL assembly, but neither first created the vulnerable request pipeline.

The older @nguniversal Express history was separately traced: 77e298adf6fdbf8cb618879626eacf57b90232ac introduced an earlier Host-derived absolute URL, decomposable through PR #897 members 7aab17675720f28fc2d4683ee00e992cd803f126 and 28932add3637f4dca352212e8a582e9f27f9b99d; that legacy implementation was later removed, so it is not the surviving current-lineage BIC reversed by the 2026 fix.

git show 6cf621c905de4815b1e12964fb909876ca6e3ea3 adds validateRequest/validateUrl and strict host, protocol, and numeric-port checks, validates CommonEngine render URLs, patches exposed request-header access, and rejects or falls back from invalid/disallowed origins; its parent 9c2ddfe187a37880708bba011dc8fe83cca2e748 lacks these validation hooks.

Release topology checks show the BIC is already in 19.0.0-next.0 and 19.0.0. Backports 2a72d7483d87ccdcfa0c5148f34a4c6ebb6c6cf9, 67582a946808d2c021cbcfacbf203ef58a6fbded, e4d445ec674841dd1d374c83344c0a704ee3807c, and f78f38827861cf01471e30fcf81ef14d6265a0f2 are excluded respectively from v19.2.20, v20.3.16, v21.1.4, and v21.2.0-rc.0 but contained in patched v19.2.21, v20.3.17, v21.1.5, and v21.2.0-rc.1; f78f38827861cf01471e30fcf81ef14d6265a0f2 explicitly states it was cherry-picked from direct fix 6cf621c905de4815b1e12964fb909876ca6e3ea3.
reasoning: The official advisory and fix describe one causal mechanism: attacker-controlled request headers became the SSR base origin, which relative HttpClient resolution and REQUEST-consuming application code could use as an outbound destination. The current affected pipeline was first written atomically by 3c9697a8c34a5e0f3470bde73f11f9f32107f42e; direct inspection proves the relevant files absent from its immediate parent, and later proxy/header commits merely modified the already-vulnerable flow. The 2026 direct fix validates precisely that origin and the exposed host headers, while four release backports align exactly with the advisory's patched boundaries. Although the repository contains an older removed @nguniversal implementation of the same idea, it is a separate predecessor rather than the surviving source-to-fix lineage. The selected BIC has only human commit-object identities and no AI marker, so the real vulnerability is NOT_AI.
